threads.body: The util tests cover the event at the shared `GenAIInvocation` level, but there’s only one end-to-end instrumentation test for it: a synchronous, non-streaming LangChain authentication failure. It would be good to add a few assertions to existing async and streaming error tests as well. Those wrappers have their own error and finalization paths, so this would confirm the original exception reaches `invocation.fail()` and the event is emitted exactly once in real instrumentation usage.

replies.body: Added checks to the Portkey async and Bedrock sync streaming error tests to confirm the event is emitted once with the right type.

threads.body: Could these tests live in `test_utils_events.py` instead? That file already covers event emission and uses essentially the same telemetry setup. Since this is another event type rather than a separate subsystem, keeping the coverage together would make the tests easier to discover and avoid creating a new file for each event scenario.

replies.body: Moved them into test_utils_events.py and reused its setup, and removed the separate file on new commit.

threads.body:
Semconv is moving to per-operation exception events (`gen_ai.client.inference.exception` in open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai#658, `gen_ai.client.embeddings.exception` in #659), with `gen_ai.client.operation.exception` left for the rest. Please make the event name a class attribute that each client invocation sets, so the rename is a one-line change per subclass.

This also replaces the `SpanKind.CLIENT` check: span kind is only a proxy for "this operation has a client exception event", and the new `_span_kind` field can go.

```python
# GenAIInvocation
_exception_event_name: ClassVar[str | None] = None

# InferenceInvocation, EmbeddingInvocation, RetrievalInvocation,
# FetchResponseInvocation, RemoteAgentInvocation
_exception_event_name: ClassVar[str | None] = "gen_ai.client.operation.exception"
```

With a per-class event name this becomes the only gate. `_start_span` is never `False` here, since the suppressed invocations override `_finish` and never call this method:

```suggestion
            self._exception_event_name is None
```

and `_EXCEPTION_EVENT_NAME` below becomes `self._exception_event_name`.

The SDK fills `exception.type`, `exception.message` and `exception.stacktrace` (same values as here) when the exception is passed to `emit`, so this can be:

```suggestion
        self._logger.emit(
            event_name=_EXCEPTION_EVENT_NAME,
            exception=exception,
            context=self._span_context,
            severity_number=SeverityNumber.WARN,
        )
```

The `traceback`, `exception_attributes` and `fq_exception_type` imports are then unused.

threads.body:
With per-operation events this needs an update:

```suggestion
When an inference, embeddings, retrieval, fetch response, agent invocation, or tool execution
operation fails with an exception, the package also emits the operation's exception event (for
example ``gen_ai.client.inference.exception``) with ``WARN`` severity, carrying ``exception.type``,
``exception.message``, and ``exception.stacktrace``. ``exception.message`` may contain sensitive
information. The event is not emitted for failures reported without an exception, or for a
``BaseException`` that is not an ``Exception``, such as cancellation.
```
